scenarios: a three-call task under a signed registry: GetTaskEconomics prices every call (USD, the registry generation) and cost_minor equals what the provider billed; one run whose steps each hold one call and add up to the task's tokens, cost and tool calls; the steps' request ids are exactly the provider's
an invoice built from the scripted provider's own record reconciles exactly (three MATCHED, delta 0, each attributed to its run)
a row with 3% more input is OUT_OF_TOLERANCE at 100 bp and within at 500 bp
a row the log never saw is NOT_IN_LOG and a call left off the invoice NOT_ON_INVOICE; a non-sample payload is refused BAD_INVOICE
audit: IMPLEMENTED-PARTIAL with drift: GetTaskEconomics summed usage reported or not and priced the whole task at the last model's catalog list price; nothing attributed usage to steps or compared an invoice with the log.
proof: Real Core with a signed registry and a scripted provider: a per-call ledger priced per binding in minor units, attributed per run and step with tool and verification time, reconciled row by row against the provider's own record within a tolerance.
negative_proof: Reconciling without the tolerance comparison accepts a 3%-over row and fails the test; the catalog estimate priced at the answered model (not the binding) failed three existing tests and was corrected before merge.
limitations: Side questions append nothing (QUAL-EV-0261) so their invoice rows are NOT_IN_LOG; no provider billing-export adapter; cache-write tokens not on ModelUsageRecorded; no registry means unpriced.

ci.note: every job green on macOS, Linux and Windows on the first attempt of the final rebase (earlier all-green runs were superseded by rebases onto main)
